title: Jeju uprising and massacres
summary: On 3 April 1948 an armed uprising began on Jeju Island, South Korea, against a separate southern government. A counterinsurgency by police, army and paramilitary groups followed, lasting until 1954 with mass arrests, forced relocations and killings of civilians. A 2003 government truth commission estimated 25,000 to 30,000 civilians killed.

uncertainty.note: Scholarship dates the broader conflict 1947-1954; the uprising itself began 3 April 1948 and the Korea.net account ends the violence on 21 September 1954.

where.historical_name: Jeju Island (Cheju-do), South Korea (US Army Military Government, then Republic of Korea)

importance.justification: One of Korea's worst civilian massacres, suppressed for decades, whose official recognition shaped South Korea's transitional justice.

audience_note: Describes mass killings of civilians, including women and children, torture and forced relocation. Death figures are estimates.

beats.caption: An armed uprising began on Jeju on 3 April 1948 against the establishment of a separate government in the south.
Counterinsurgency by police, military and paramilitaries, with mass arrests and relocations, continued until 21 September 1954, when the Hallasan lockdown was lifted.
A 2003 government commission found excessive force and estimated 25,000 to 30,000 civilians killed on Jeju.
